source_row.stem: A nurse reviews a peripheral blood smear report noting "microcytic, hypochromic" red blood cells, and a nursing student assumes this description sounds like it would fit a vitamin B12 deficiency picture. This description is instead most consistent with:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Normal red blood cell morphology typically expected on a routine peripheral blood smear, contrary to what this particular abnormal description actually reflects","B":"Iron deficiency anemia, characterized by smaller, paler-than-normal red blood cells, rather than the B12 deficiency picture the student is currently assuming this description fits","C":"Macrocytic anemia, a pattern generally associated with larger rather than smaller red blood cells, which is the opposite of the microcytic pattern actually described here","D":"A finding generally considered unrelated to any underlying anemia or red cell abnormality, contrary to what this particular smear description actually indicates"}}
source_row.rationale: Microcytic (small) and hypochromic (pale, low hemoglobin content) red blood cells on a peripheral smear are classic morphologic findings of iron deficiency anemia.
source_row.source_name: Clinical Hematology References — RBC Morphology Terminology
